lesson.subtitle: Lesson 12 -- Read the Beach
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato | Lesson 12 -- Read the Beach

listenings.text: Right, the report for Tuesday. There is three feet of clean swell on the south coast and the wind is offshore until about ten. If you get down there early, you will have the best two hours of the week. After ten it turns onshore and it will be a mess by lunchtime, so do not plan a long session. One warning for the beaches up north. The patrol is only on from nine, and there is a strong current running along the sandbank at the moment. If you paddle out before nine, nobody will be watching you. If you are not sure, go south.

Hi love, it is me. Quick one before you leave for the beach. There is sunscreen in the blue bag by the door. If you forget it, you will regret it by two o'clock, I promise you. Second thing. The water has been really warm this week, so if you see anything in the water that looks like a plastic bag, get out. That is a jellyfish, and it will hurt for hours. And listen, if the yellow sign is up at the top of the steps, do not go in. Just come home and we will go tomorrow. Text me when you get there.

paras: Swim and surf between the red and yellow flags. If you go outside them, the patrol will not see you, and nobody will come. The lifeguards move the flags every morning, so look for them before you go in.
Read the signs at the top of the steps. A yellow sign is a warning: there is a hazard in the water today. If the sign says strong current, you will feel it as soon as you are past your waist.
If a rip takes you, do not swim against it. You will get tired in under a minute. Float, raise one arm and signal to the patrol. If you stay with your board, we will find you faster.

Two more things. If the water is warm and flat in January, there will be jellyfish, so ask at the tower before you go in. And put sunscreen on before you leave the house. If you wait until you are on the sand, you will forget.
